items.title: watchOS 27.3 Brings Live Rewind and Siri Recap to Apple Watch
items.snippet: With the first beta of watchOS 27.3, Apple is introducing new Audio Intelligence features it previewed for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 earlier this year. Powered by the S11 chip, Audio Intelligence includes Live Rewind, Siri Recap, Sound Recognition, and Shazam Music Recognition. Sound Recognition and Shazam are already on the watch, but Live Rewind and ‌Siri‌ Recap are now available in the beta. Live Rewind can show you a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. If you miss something like a waiter giving you the daily specials at a restaurant, you can press twice on the Digital Crown to see what was said without having to ask the person to repeat themselves.

items.title: iPhone Duo Gets Reachability in iOS 27.3 Beta
items.snippet: With today's iOS 27.3 beta, Apple expanded Reachability to the iPhone Duo . Reachability lets ‌iPhone Duo‌ users shift the content on the left or right side of the outer screen to make it easier to reach with a thumb. Reachability can be turned on or off by going to Settings > Accessibility > Touch > Reachability. It is on by default after updating to the new software. When the ‌iPhone Duo‌ is closed, a short swipe left on the left edge or a short swipe right on the right edge will shift the outer display's content left or right. items.title: Sam Altman meets with Samsung leadership to secure more RAM for data centers amid crushing shortages

items.title: Network appliances go more than a year without patches as exploits speed up
items.snippet: The median vulnerability on enterprise network appliances stays unpatched for more than a year, Microsoft’s own telemetry shows, even as the most damaging software flaws are being weaponized within days of disclosure. Microsoft Security Research reported the findings Monday in an analysis of roughly 383,000 CVEs disclosed from 1999 through September 2026. It shows that the median time to patch a vulnerability exceeds a year for network appliances. items.title: NaaS hasn’t lived up to the hype. Is it still worth it?
items.snippet: In 2021, Gartner expected a promising future for Network as a Service (NaaS). At the time, adoption accounted for less than 1% of enterprises, and Gartner expected that number to rise to 15% by 2024. Instead, in Gartner’s latest hype cycle for networking , NaaS is still at 1% to 5% market penetration. That’s short of Gartner’s earlier expectations. In fact, Gartner places NaaS deep in the “trough of disillusionment” in its 2026 Hype Cycle for Enterprise Networking. items.title: AI networking spending grows, but enterprise network readiness lags
items.snippet: Spending for AI buildout has reached shocking scale, though much of the spending comes from hyperscalers and neocloud providers. Enterprises are, however, still in the mix, with networking being one of the core elements of spend. Networking vendors are still seeing growth. Dell’Oro Group reports that worldwide enterprise networkin g revenue grew 15% year over year in the first half of 2026 .
